protocol.symmetry_reduction: None: all16layer pairs at both returns and both presets are rendered. Simultaneous half-cycle inversion is checked afterward without omitting states.
protocol.oscillator_scope: Each layer's two classic oscillators share that layer's waveform-origin shift. Normal clocks/note-to-note phase behavior remain unchanged; individual oscillator-relative phases are untested.
protocol.build_strategy: Two isolated frozen renderers, differing only in previous0.8 versus half0.4 wet return. Two explicit audit environment values are read once per process and select the Upper/Lower origins. Shipping source/API untouched.

const double phaseOffset1 = classicParameter (wave1, timbre_.phaseCycles, 0.0);

protocol.calibration: One previous-return prefix envelope lag bounded±50ms and one prefix RMS gain PER phase; freeze both across the previous/half pair. No candidate-specific gain, no per-note phase/timing fit.
protocol.evaluation: Primary keeps original per-case split, with identical later support inside each phase pair. Conservative cross-phase-support diagnostic uses reference[cal+2205:n-2205], chosen before scores from the allowed lag bound; no frame crosses calibration.
protocol.objectives: Retain all five existing summary errors, full measures and reference-only activity-mask diagnostics for every phase/return; no phase is selected. Paired half-minus-previous changes are descriptive.
protocol.controls: All four diagonal common phases at both returns/presets must reproduce the earlier16WAVs and metrics exactly; this includes the original zero-phase fourWAV controls.
protocol.limits: No phase selection or source/candidate matching. Two fixed reconstructed DUAL performances; recorded raw revision/controllers/capture and exact performance unknown. Grid does not bound all phases, especially individual oscillator phases.

inherited_source_audit.accumulation: One already panned/leveled voice sample l/r enters dry once and each effect bus once multiplied by that voice's depth/127. Part enable, expression, tone balance and patch level precede both dry/send paths; no extra DUAL-only gain in accumulation. Reverb takes the summed stereo send and summed wet delay once.
inherited_source_audit.cancellation: D=U+L while direct reverb input uses sU*U+sL*L. Unequal sends mean phase cancellation in dry need not cancel the effects input; this is a signal relationship, not evidence of a DUAL scaling bug.
inherited_source_audit.policy: reset initializes classic clocks to0 once; note triggering does not reset them. Classic waveform-origin offsets preserve that note-to-note policy, while shifting waveform and BLEP/BLAMP together. Both selected presets use MIX, so canonical SYNC clock is not involved.
inherited_source_audit.limits: Code inspection rules out an obvious extra DUAL-only multiplier, not an unmeasured Roland layer/headroom/send conversion.

case.title: Club Bass — separated opening bass reconstruction
case.method: Hardware-only spectrograms show a low D1 family near 36.7 Hz together with components near 73.4 and 293 Hz. The original patch maps a played key to Lower oscillators at −12, Upper triangle at 0, and Upper sine at +24 semitones, so the first three keys are MIDI 38 (D2). Later 43.65/87.3/349 Hz families identify MIDI 41 (F2), followed by two more D2 events. Onsets, repeated-note renewals, and gates were read from the audio waveform and spectral changes without fitting to Septum.
uncertainties: Original performance MIDI is unavailable; this is a source-audio reconstruction, not a recovered original performance.
All velocities are fixed to 100 as an explicit unknown placeholder; no velocity, preset parameter, or recording EQ was fitted to Septum output.

Played-note inference assumes default system transpose and the documented/current WIDE-dependent oscillator ranges. Original system settings, controller events, exact recorded patch revision, and recording processing are unknown.
Event times refer to decoded MP3 audio. Hardware latency, encoder history, oscillator state, and effect history are not recovered; no post-render alignment or time warping is implied.
Onsets and gates are approximate within 10–20 ms. The F-to-D transition may contain a short overlap; note-off and note-on are placed together as an explicit estimate.
The original Lower tone has SOLO LEGATO and portamento enabled, so overlap uncertainty can affect the F-to-D transition. The first three separated D notes are the strongest timing evidence.
Upper filter LFO, overdrive, and original reverb remain enabled. The residual reverb tail is retained in the crop and is not interpreted as additional MIDI notes.

case.title: Ambient SQR — nominal gates, velocity 100
case.method: Source-only original MP3 inspection: native stereo spectra, fundamental and odd-harmonic families in three fixed plateaus, short RMS history and time-frequency transitions. Dominant families near 587, 659, 698 Hz support played MIDI 74, 76, 77 under the unchanged published preset's zero coarse/octave and zero pitch-envelope/LFO depths. Nominal key-ups follow envelope roll-off near the observed level maxima, with broad operational uncertainty; they are not recovered release events. No engine or candidate scores were used. This is an operational gate/velocity sensitivity derived from the frozen source-only reconstruction; no new note transcription or candidate-based fit.
uncertainties: Original MIDI, velocity, controllers, global transpose/tuning, output latency/capture chain and exact recorded patch revision are unavailable. The MP3 and bank are associated by Roland name/category.

Velocity 100 is nominal. Upper AMP velocity sensitivity is 0, Lower is 8; both cutoff velocity sensitivities are 0. Velocity can alter the layer and wet/dry balance, so a common scalar gain does not remove its uncertainty.

Upper has two Squares, drive 30, Solo Legato and portamento 20; Lower has two Sines, slower AMP attack 76 and Solo without portamento. Old-note energy may be release, delay or reverb; it does not prove held-key overlap.

Onset ranges are operational source-clock reconstruction uncertainties, not certified MIDI time bounds. A later production-only prefix alignment may absorb one common latency; do not tune later notes to candidate errors.

Key-up estimates near envelope maxima are provisional: the amplitude/filter envelopes, two layers, drive, interference and wet tails prevent uniquely recovering key release. Off-time ranges are sensitivity settings, not confidence intervals or observed gates.
The 0.775-second crop excludes the next obvious new pitch group near 0.79 s. The third note's gate is still estimated; later hardware decay is not covered by this short reconstruction.

All three original notes and preceding silence are retained from source time 0 for effect history. Exact published SysEx must remain unchanged. This is a conditional generalization case, not an output-equivalence benchmark.

validation_plan.comparison_policy: One production-only prefix lag and gain; freeze for the later E5/F5 region. Any velocity/gate sensitivity must be predeclared, reported in full and applied equally to all DSP candidates without selecting its best error. Keep original SysEx unchanged.
validation_plan.gate_sensitivity_suggestion: Nominal key-ups; then all early endpoints; then all late endpoints from each note's off_sensitivity_seconds. These bracket plausible articulation without recovering it.

sensitivity.policy: All nine predeclared combinations; same inputs to every frozen DSP candidate. No scenario selection by model error.

limits: Grid outcomes are deterministic sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals or bounds over continuous phase.
All16 layer states were rendered, but simultaneous half-cycle inversion makes only eight distinct magnitude responses for each preset/return.
Each layer has one common origin; individual within-layer oscillator phases and hardware phase reset/randomness remain untested.
